title: ForageScan
shortDescription: Identify edible mushrooms and avoid toxic lookalikes with image recognition.
fullDescription: A mobile app that uses image recognition to identify edible mushrooms and flag toxic lookalikes. Offline mode, an in-app journal and community review support safe, educated foraging.
reflection: The Forage Scan project demonstrated how design can bridge safety, education, and community in nature-based activities. By offering dependable image identification, professional input, and offline accessibility, the system immediately addressed the problem of safe foraging. Future improvements will include community features to promote knowledge-sharing, and adding seasonal identification recommendations to improve user experience. The project proved the importance of making design decisions based on research when creating practical, user-centred digital solutions.

title: TutorAid
tagline: Connecting students with reliable tutors for academic success.
shortDescription: Connects students with reliable tutors for academic support.
fullDescription: A React web app where students search for tutors by subject, availability and rating, then message and book sessions. Tutors build profiles that show their expertise and teaching style.
reflection: This project was a full journey for me, not just in building a product, but in learning how to think like a full-stack developer. One of the biggest learning curves was setting up and maintaining the SQL database and ensuring secure communication between the frontend and backend. I also had to learn how to deploy both sides of the app separately, which required research, patience, and LOTS of trial-and-error. Through this, I really improved my debugging skills, my understanding of server-client communication, and how to optimise code for performance and loading speed.
role: Solo: chose the theme, designed UX, UI and API, built the full-stack system
highlights: Based on real tutor challenges: booking and time management
Secure, usable full-stack build with brand and deployment
Frontend, backend and database all delivered

title: Disney+ Finder
tagline: Discover the best of Disney+ with ease.
shortDescription: Discover high-quality Disney+ titles by rating, not endless scrolling.
fullDescription: A React app that combines a curated Disney+ dataset with OMDb ratings and metadata. Users filter, sort and compare titles to quickly choose what to watch.
reflection: This project was a masterclass in frontend adaptability and problem-solving. When faced with a highly restrictive and poorly documented Disney Plus API that bottlenecked development, I strategically pivoted to the OMDB API, instantly restoring data reliability and fetch consistency. Alongside this backend migration, I overcame several UI/UX hurdles—refining CSS for optimal dropdown legibility, engineering a custom JavaScript alert system, and meticulously mapping data fields into Chart.js to create a highly responsive, visually engaging comparison tool.
highlights: Pivoted from a restrictive Disney+ API to OMDb to keep data reliable
Chart.js comparison charts and a custom alert system
Multi-page navigation with React Router

title: Psychedelic Pixels
tagline: Celebrating the bizarre and extraordinary in art.
shortDescription: An e-commerce site for unconventional, surreal and imaginative art.
fullDescription: An online gallery and store for bold, offbeat artwork. It connects eccentric artists with collectors who want something unlike a traditional gallery.
reflection: This project was a deep dive into the world of e-commerce development, and it taught me a lot about the complexities of building a platform that can handle product listings, user accounts, and secure transactions. One of the biggest challenges was integrating a payment gateway, which required me to learn about security best practices and how to handle sensitive user data. I also had to learn how to manage state effectively in a React application with multiple components and user interactions. Overall, this project was a great learning experience that helped me develop my skills in both frontend and backend development.
role: Team of three: admin pages and checkout
team: André van Heerden: login and authentication
Gaby Norris: admin pages and checkout
highlights: MERN-stack e-commerce build with a strong brand identity
Extra features beyond the standard brief

title: Spoonful
tagline: Loud but classy: a brand for Broadway lovers.
shortDescription: A design system for a Broadway-inspired cuisine festival.
fullDescription: A design system that unifies the festival's identity across digital and print, with an earthy, vintage tone that blends food, music and theatre.
reflection: A consistent and welcoming visual identity that connected digital and physical interactions was created with the Spoonful design system. The system effectively captured the cosiness and theatrical quality of the festival through the use of earthy tones, retro-inspired font, and modular elements. The study showed how using consistent design principles may improve user engagement across several touchpoints and build brand identification. Expanding accessibility rules, including motion design to enhance interactivity, and evaluating the scalability of system components across printed goods and social media campaigns are some of the upcoming enhancements.
highlights: Vision: loud but classy, built for a magical night of impromptu performances
Mission: bring all Broadway enthusiasts together
Tone of voice: enthusiastic, welcoming, witty and trustworthy
Full system: brand strategy, atoms, molecules, organisms and wireframes

title: Nia
shortDescription: Nia: an AI-assisted wearable ecosystem for focus and productivity.
fullDescription: Nia (Swahili for purpose) is a wearable AI ecosystem that helps focused professionals spot invisible overload and offload mental residue after work. A smartwatch reads heart rate and work activity, then nudges the user with gentle haptics while they stay in control.
reflection: How do we stop professional burnout without driving users crazy? By pairing wearable heart rate tracking with desktop app monitoring, the ecosystem catches the exact moment deep focus turns into stressful frustration. Instead of forcing interruptions, it sends a gentle wrist buzz for a break and offers a quick voice brain dump to clear your head. The biggest lesson was finding the line between helpful tracking and feeling spied on. Our research showed that monitoring biometrics and screens feels like surveillance without strict boundaries. We solved this by building absolute user control directly into the interface, allowing anyone to manually set their focus baseline, choose tracked apps, or completely turn off break prompts.
role: Solo: research, UX and UI design
highlights: How might we help professionals recognise invisible overload in real time, while keeping human agency?
Persona: Misha, a full-stack developer who can't switch off after work
Features: stress detection, brain-dump voice notes, smart break timing and focus-state tracking
Usability testing fixed loops in onboarding, missing device pairing and information overload
Zero-cloud approach and per-app tracking controls to protect privacy

title: MasterChef Broadway
tagline: A responsive website that brings the excitement of a Broadway-inspired culinary festival to life.
shortDescription: A responsive website for a Broadway-inspired culinary festival.
fullDescription: The festival's digital hub, covering event info, participating chefs and performers, and interactive features. Its design blends theatre and gastronomy.
reflection: Spoonful's brand activation, MasterChef Broadway and responsive website successfully combined culinary performance with theatrical spectacle.  The three phases of the activation (before, during, and after the event), provided viewers with continuous opportunities to interact with the brand.  Future improvements include expanding accessibility features, adding VR or live streaming for remote participation, and turning the website into a year-round engagement hub that sustains community interest outside of the festival.
highlights: Digital hub for the festival: chefs, performers, dishes and results
Winner announcement and visitor reviews built into the experience
Theatre and gastronomy blended into one brand
